title: The Circular Flow of Income
summary: The participants in the economy (households, businesses, government and the foreign sector), the markets that connect them, and the flows of goods, services, factors and money.

rows: Own the factors of production (land, labour, capital, entrepreneurship), sell them to businesses and buy goods and services
Buy factors of production, produce goods and services and sell them
Collects taxes, provides public goods and services, buys from businesses and employs workers
Other countries that buy our exports and sell us imports

items: **Goods (product) market**: where goods and services are bought and sold (shops, online stores).
**Factor market**: where factors of production are bought and sold (e.g. the labour market where people find jobs).
**Financial market**: where savings and loans are made (banks, the stock exchange).

notes.caption: Solid lines: real flows (factors, goods and services). Dashed lines: money flows (income and spending).

notes.text: There are two types of flow, moving in **opposite directions**:

items: **Real flow**: factors of production go from households to businesses; goods and services go from businesses to households.
**Money flow**: businesses pay households **income** (rent, wages, interest and profit); households pay businesses for goods and services (**consumer spending**).

notes.text: Adding the government and the foreign sector

rows: Government → businesses and households (salaries, grants, buying goods)
Financial market → businesses (loans to buy capital)

notes.label: Key idea
notes.text: If **injections** (government spending, investment, exports) are greater than **leakages** (taxes, savings, imports), the economy grows. If leakages are greater, the economy shrinks.

notes.title: Tracing the flow
notes.problem: Nomsa works at a clothing factory and earns R8 000 a month. She pays R600 tax, saves R400 and spends the rest at local shops. Identify the flows.
steps: Nomsa (household) sells labour to the factory (business) in the factor market and receives wages: real flow and money flow.
R600 tax goes to government: a leakage.
R400 savings go to the bank (financial market): a leakage.
R7 000 is spent in the goods market: consumer spending flows to businesses.
notes.answer: Income R8 000; leakages R1 000; spending R7 000

notes.title: Leakages and injections
notes.problem: Classify each as a leakage from, or an injection into, the circular flow: household savings, government spending on roads, income tax, exports, imports.
steps: A leakage takes money out of the flow: savings, taxes and imports.
An injection puts money in: investment, government spending and exports.
notes.answer: Leakages: savings, income tax and imports. Injections: government spending and exports.
